title: Normalize /v1/chat.completions stop/logprob negotiation, add stream heartbeat and JSON-response mode
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Stabilizes OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity for stop/logprobs in streaming mode, introduces a lightweight stream heartbeat to prevent stalled TCP connections, and adds an opt-in JSON-response mode to better support schema-constrained tool outputs.
description:
Motivation: Several customer tickets and internal evaluations showed two classes of failures when using the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions endpoint: (1) mismatched stop parameter formats (string vs array) that produced inconsistent stream envelopes and premature token truncation, and (2) intermittent stalled streams when clients kept idle sockets open (notably mobile clients behind aggressive NAT). Additionally, we need a safer way to signal structured outputs for tool-calling workflows without forcing the full function-calling handshake. This PR aims to: 1) normalize stop parameter handling across the adapter and streaming layer, mapping single-string stops to an array and documenting behavior; 2) stop/logprobs negotiation: explicitly encode when token-level logprobs are requested so the streaming envelope includes logprob frames consistently and avoids mixed-mode frames; 3) add a lightweight heartbeat frame for the streaming protocol to keep intermediate idle connections alive and provide an explicit 'stream-alive' event to clients; 4) introduce an opt-in "json_mode" flag that wraps assistant text in a top-level JSON envelope for schema-first tools while preserving streaming token granularity.

What changed (high level):
- API adapter: src/adapter/openai_v1_compat.py — central logic that normalizes incoming request params (stop(s), max_tokens priority, logprobs boolean vs integer) and emits a canonical internal request shape. Single-string stop -> [stop]. If stop is empty/null, adapter leaves it unset.
- Streaming runtime: src/runtime/stream_muxer.go — implement heartbeat frame type ("HB") emitted every 15s of inactivity per connection, plus explicit frame type for Logprob toggles so clients can parse token frames deterministically.
- Runtime token envelope: protocol change to include "meta" frames before stream tokens when properties such as logprobs or role-normalization change mid-stream. This avoids ambiguous tokens when a fallback or model variant is used.
- SDK changes: sdk/js/src/chat.ts and sdk/python/redwood/chat_client.py add support for feeding heartbeat frames to the event parser and a new option "json_mode: 'off'|'opt-in'|'strict'" (default off). When opt-in, the server emits a final JSON-body frame labeled "json-result" with the assembled assistant text parsed as JSON if it validates against a coarse JSON sanity check.
- Docs: docs/openai_compat/chat-parity-stop-logprob.md — documents normalized behavior and examples (single stop string -> array, example streaming event sequences with heartbeat and logprob frames, json_mode semantics).
- Tests: tests/compat/test_chat_streaming_stop_logprob.py and integration/e2e_chat_jsonmode.py with new fixtures for fragmented stop tokens and delayed client ack scenarios.

Commits (summary):
- Normalize incoming stop param and add unit tests (Aisha K.)
- Introduce stream heartbeat frames and heartbeat handler in muxer (Diego M.)
- Add logprob negotiation flag and consistent envelope headers (Aisha K.)
- JS/Python SDK support for heartbeat and json_mode (Sofia C.)
- Docs and examples + compatibility test matrix (Tomislav H.)

Files changed (high-level):
- src/adapter/openai_v1_compat.py (adapter param normalization, new tests)
- src/runtime/stream_muxer.go (heartbeat emitter, frame types)
- src/runtime/token_envelope.go (meta frame handling)
- sdk/js/src/chat.ts (event parser upgrade, json_mode opt-in)
- sdk/python/redwood/chat_client.py (json_mode flag, heartbeat glue)
- docs/openai_compat/chat-parity-stop-logprob.md (compat docs)
- tests/compat/test_chat_streaming_stop_logprob.py (unit tests)
- integration/e2e_chat_jsonmode.py (integration test)
- tools/benchmarks/stream-liveness-check.sh (small test harness)

Testing and CI: The PR initially had two flaky failures in streaming unit tests caused by race between the heartbeat ticker and test harness teardown. I pushed a follow-up commit to make the test harness deterministic by injecting a mock clock into the muxer during tests. After that, the full CI (unit, integration, lint, mypy/ruff for python, ts-jest for JS) passed. Local manual verification performed with a mobile-like NAT emulator confirmed the heartbeat prevented mid-stream stall for a simulated 60s idle period; memory/CPU overhead of the heartbeat was negligible in perf runs.

Review notes and conversation (selected):
- Diego Morales: "We should avoid exposing heartbeat frames at the HTTP/1 SSE boundary if some clients rely on text/event-stream parsing semantics; consider falling back to NOP comments." Reply (Aisha): "Good point — adapter will emit heartbeat as a comment line for SSE clients and as explicit HB frames on our binary websocket framing. Added a conditional encoder for SSE in stream_muxer.go." Status: resolved.
- Sofia Chen: "What about clients expecting logprobs as integer depth (n) rather than boolean?" Reply (Aisha): "Adapter accepts both boolean and integer for logprobs; if integer>0 we request up to that depth and annotate the stream meta frame with exact depth. Docs updated with example." Status: addressed.
- Tomislav Horvat: "json_mode strict could break existing text consumers if enabled accidentally. Make it opt-in and require explicit Content-Type: application/json+schema in request header." Reply (Aisha): "Implemented as opt-in only; strict mode additionally requires header hint and will fail fast if the final payload is not valid JSON." Status: addressed.

Backward compatibility: The adapter preserves existing defaults — old clients that post string stop or array stop get normalized behavior with no functional change except improved consistency in streaming envelopes. Heartbeat frames are invisible to most SDKs unless they opt into the parser change; SDKs were updated in this PR. json_mode is opt-in and will not change default responses.

Security and performance: No secrets handling changes. Heartbeat adds a tiny per-connection timer; bench runs show <0.5% CPU at 1000 concurrent idle streams. json_mode sanitizes final payload with a coarse JSON parse; strict mode does additional schema validation which is off by default to avoid CPU spikes.

Follow-ups (future work tracked in ENG-7819):
- Add a formal schema registry for json_mode strict validation and tie to function-call tool specs.
- Consider TTL-based heartbeat tuning (adaptive intervals) for mobile.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after final approval by Diego and Sofia. Changelog entry added to docs/releases/2024-10.md.

If you want to reproduce: see docs/openai_compat/README for quick steps and the new integration test which demonstrates a fragmented stop token scenario with streaming logprob frames and shows reconstructed JSON output when json_mode is opt-in.
notes: This PR targets parity work for OpenAI /v1/chat.completions while avoiding breaking user expectations. The approach taken emphasizes explicit negotiation frames and opt-in structured output to keep compatibility surface minimal.
